paragraphs: Friend, here's what gets me about this passage. Josiah hears the Book of the Covenant, and he doesn't just feel bad about it. He reads it in the hearing of all the people, stands by the pillar, and makes a covenant before the LORD "to follow the LORD and to keep His commandments, decrees, and statutes with all his heart and all his soul" (2 Kings 23:2-3). Hearing God's Word was never meant to stop at the ears. It's meant to move your hands and your feet.

Now look at how far he goes. Altars on the roof, horses at the LORD's front door, high places from Geba to Beersheba, and he keeps going until he's cleared out everything that competed with the LORD (2 Kings 23:4-14). Papa Dorin has a few little habits in his own bakery that should've been cleaned out years ago, and I keep saying I'll get to them LATER. Josiah shows us that real obedience doesn't clean one corner and call it a day. It asks, "What else in here is taking God's place?"

And one more thing, baker. Even in the middle of all that tearing down, Josiah stops at one tomb and says, "Let him rest" (2 Kings 23:18). He remembered the man of God who had spoken the LORD's word, and he honored it. When God's Word gets into a heart, it makes room for what God has said and clears out what He hasn't. Josiah's story isn't over yet, so keep your oven warm.
